summary: MariaDB is configured on node1 and verified after a full node restart. The generated credential was not disclosed.
actions_performed: Created the inventory database and InnoDB items table.
Created inventory_app@localhost with SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE privileges on inventory.*.
Generated the account password on node1 and stored connection variables in /etc/inventory-db.env as root:root mode 0600.
Authenticated with the stored credential and persisted a restart-proof row.
Restarted node1 exactly once and verified MariaDB, schema, account, credential permissions, and data recovery.

evidence.requirement: MariaDB service is enabled, active, and restart-persistent
evidence.summary: MariaDB was active and enabled before and after the node restart; post-restart mariadb-admin reported mysqld alive.

evidence.requirement: inventory database and items table exist and are usable
evidence.summary: Direct metadata confirmed inventory.items as InnoDB, authenticated application CRUD succeeded, and the table plus durable row survived restart.

evidence.requirement: Local application account and protected generated credential
evidence.summary: inventory_app exists only at localhost with four scoped data privileges. /etc/inventory-db.env is root:root mode 0600, non-root reading was denied, and its credential authenticated successfully before and after restart.

Healthy baseline boot ID c2ffc729-a31e-486e-95de-cf2023dea95c was captured, systemd acknowledged the reboot, the new boot ID 66b5f139-6396-4136-a674-56d486f57c7a proved a node restart, and full service/data recovery was verified.
